title: Flexbox Lab: direction, wrap, alignment, grow/shrink
learningObjectives: Explain flexbox lab: direction, wrap, alignment, grow/shrink and design an accessible interactive learning lab.

understand.concept: A Flexbox Lab exposes direction, wrapping, justify-content, align-items, align-content, gap, and per-item grow, shrink, and basis controls. It should render a live preview and display the generated CSS declarations.
understand.whyItMatters: The lab should distinguish container properties from item properties, support keyboard controls, and let learners test narrow containers and long labels. A single example should not imply that one flex configuration suits every layout.
understand.analogy: The lab is a row-and-column workbench where learners adjust how items share and align within available space.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports understanding; a production lab needs real state management, safe preview isolation, and accessible controls.

explain.narrative: The starter shows wrapping, distribution, alignment, and gap. Interactive controls and per-item sizing are the build task.

examples.explanation: The starter shows wrapping, distribution, alignment, and gap. Interactive controls and per-item sizing are the build task.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered starter preview for the interactive lab concept.

practise.guidedTask: Add controls for flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, and gap. Add grow/shrink/basis controls for one selected item and show the generated CSS.
practise.independentTask: Implement the lab with labelled controls, a live preview, validation, reset behaviour, and a generated CSS readout. Test keyboard and mobile operation.
hints: Keep preview state and code output synchronized.
Handle invalid input without crashing the lab.
Keep learner content isolated from the parent application.

practice.starterCode: OneTwoThree
practice.resetCode: OneTwoThree

questions.prompt: Which controls should be available at the container level in a Flexbox Lab?
options: Direction, wrap, justify-content, align-items, and gap
questions.answer: Direction, wrap, justify-content, align-items, and gap
questions.explanation: These configure the overall flex container; grow, shrink, and basis belong to items.

questions.prompt: What is a core quality requirement for an interactive CSS lab?
options: Accessible controls, safe validation, and synchronized output
Using innerHTML for every learner input
questions.answer: Accessible controls, safe validation, and synchronized output
questions.explanation: A learning lab must be understandable, safe, and responsive to learner input.
